intro: Step into Diyarbakır Museum, a museum in Diyarbakır province, founded in 1934. It gathers the excavations of the upper Tigris basin, with special weight on the Neolithic finds of Çayönü and on Artuqid metalwork.
history: Founded in 1934, the museum brings together the excavations of the upper Tigris basin. The Çayönü mound, in this region, is among the best documented places for humanity's passage to farming and settled life — and here the museum shows you that passage layer by layer.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the finds from Çayönü, the Assyrian and Roman works, the Artuqid metalwork and the ethnography hall.
facts: Did you know? The copper beads from Çayönü belong to the moment people first began hammering metal, around 7000 BC. This museum is the central collection for the upper Tigris excavations, and it follows the passage to farming layer by layer.
outro: This brings our tour of Diyarbakır Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. From the first farmers to the metalworkers, thank you for walking their path. Enjoy your visit.
